newsitem.title: UK: RTZ shares fall on news of Utah strike.
newsitem.headline: RTZ shares fall on news of Utah strike.

text.p: Shares in RTZ Corp Plc, the British arm of mining giant RTZ-CRA, dropped 12 pence to 972-1/2 pence on news that unionised workers at its ill-fated Kennecott copper smelter in Utah had gone on strike.
Analysts, however, did not see a major threat to results of RTZ-CRA.
"They don't have a history of long-term strikes," said Emile Morfett at Paribas.
"It's probably a flash in the pan," he said, adding that the strike would only begin to bite if it lasted for more than a couple of weeks.
RTZ, meanwhile, said the strike would not affect production.
The strike comes after the Kennecott smelter was dogged earlier this year by severe technical problems, which came on top of a sharp drop in world copper prices.

These two factors contributed to a 22 percent fall in RTZ-CRA's first-half profits, which were reported on September 12. It makes a gloomy background for the talks between Kennecott and the United Steelworkers of America Unions, which focus on wages and pensions, analysts said. "They (Kennecott) won't have so much on the table for them (the workers)," said Morfett.
